identity: Hadith. Specifically Sahih al-Bukhari, kitab al-iman, the muallaq report transmitted from Malik (bab husn islam al-mar): a four-link isnad (qala Malik > Zayd b. Aslam > Ata b. Yasar > Abu Said al-Khudri > samia rasul Allah) followed by a short prophetic matn on how good Islam wipes out prior sins and on the tenfold reckoning of good and bad deeds. This is the SAME book and the same edition family as doc_e1435023282b (kitab al-luqata), which was my worst document in batch 1 at F1 37.5. 54 tokens, a single paragraph, zero <NL> tokens, so the only forced boundary is the final token 53. My doctrine section D and LAW 6 both apply directly, and LAW 6 sets the target sentence length here at 4-9 tokens against a batch-1 bias of 20+ (catastrophic under-cutting).
law: Reconstruct the ink, not the meaning (LAW 0 corollary). For this book the punctuation model that fits every section-D observation I have is: (1) a printed comma becomes a boundary; (2) the isnad an-chain / an-X-akhbarahu link joints each carry a comma and so each transmission act is its own segment, exactly as D1 showed for hadthana X / qala hadthana Y, while a bare preposition-phrase chain (an X an Y) carries no comma and does not cut; (3) an explicative colon inside the matn becomes a boundary (section A4, J1, K3 all show colons cutting elsewhere in this corpus); (4) BUT the punctuation at a speech-verb-to-direct-quote seam was lost in this corpus (D2 gold welds faqala arif wikaaha, D3 gold welds qala fadallat al-ibil faghadiba and explicitly notes the question mark did not survive), so the colon before a quotation is unreliable; (5) inside the matn the segmentation is dense and even a TRAILING subordinate clause gets its own segment (D2 gold: thumma arrifha sanatan thumma istamti biha || fa-in jaa rabbuha fa-adiha ilayhi ||), which is the hadith-specific counterweight to LAW 4; (6) LAW 1's argument test governs every wa- joint: wa + a clause with a NEW argument cuts, wa inside a phrase or a shared-subject VP chain does not. Net target rhythm ~5-7 tokens per segment.
reasoning: STEP 0 calibration (checklist item 1): 54 tokens, register = hadith, LAW 6 target 4-9 tokens, so I should expect roughly 6-13 boundaries. My batch-1 output in this register averaged 20+ tokens per segment and scored F1 37.5 with the errors overwhelmingly MISSES. LAW 0 therefore governs: at a coin-flip site, CUT. SITE 1 (index 1, malik) NO CUT. Printed source is wa-qala Malikun: akhbarani Zaydu bnu Aslama. This is a colon, but it is a speech-verb-to-quote seam, and D1's gold shows qala welding FORWARD to its reported content (gold: hadthana Abd Allah b. Muhammad || qala hadthana Abu Amir ||, the cut lands BEFORE qala, never after it). By that symmetry qala malik + akhbarani Zayd b. Aslam is one 6-token link, structurally the exact analogue of D1's 5-token opening link hadthana Abd Allah b. Muhammad. I resist the LAW 0 reflex here because I have a positive structural reason, and my batch-1 precision was fine. SITES 5, 10, 15 (aslam, akhbarahu, akhbarahu) CUT, high confidence. These are the three isnad link joints. Each opens an-X-akhbarahu, a fresh finite clause with a new narrator NP, each carries a comma in print, and each is the Muwatta-idiom equivalent of D1's qala hadthana joint. LAW 3 reinforces site 15: an Ata b. Yasar akhbarahu / an Aba Said al-Khudri akhbarahu is pure shape repetition, and repetition always cuts. Note I deliberately do NOT cut at 9 (yasar) or 14 (al-khudri) since akhbarahu is the predicate of its own an-clause, not a new link. SITE 24 (yaqul) CUT, LOW confidence, and this is the one site I argued longest. Against: it is a speech-verb-to-quote seam with a colon, and BOTH of my section-D quote-seam observations (D2 faqala arif, D3 qala fadallat al-ibil) say the corpus lost that punctuation. For: it is a colon, it is the single most salient structural juncture in any hadith (isnad ends, matn begins), and without it segment 16-29 runs to 14 tokens, which is exactly the 20-plus failure mode that produced my 37.5. Cutting here yields annahu samia rasul Allah salla Allah alayhi wa-sallam yaqul (9 tok) || idha aslama al-abd fa-hasuna islamuhu (5 tok) || yukaffir Allah anhu kulla sayyiatin kana zalafaha (7 tok), a textbook hadith ladder. Under LAW 0 the expected cost of a miss is ~5x a false cut, so this is +EV even at well under even odds. Marked lo so a wrong call is legible to the next doctrine revision. SITE 27 (al-abd) NO CUT despite D2's cut-before-fa-plus-verb rule. fa-hasuna islamuhu is a second protasis verb inside the idha condition, not a new narrative step, and there is no comma there in print (the comma falls after islamuhu). D2's fa-cuts were all clause-initial after a COMPLETED clause. SITE 29 (islamuhu) CUT, med. Comma in print at the protasis/jawab seam. This runs against section C1 (a conditional period is one unit), but C1 came from Ibn Tufayl where the lau-la period is printed without an internal comma, so C1 is likely an artefact of absent ink rather than a rule against cutting conditionals. If I refuse both 24 and 29 the segment runs 16-36 = 21 tokens, which is indefensible in this register, so at least one of the two must fall and 29 is the better-attested one. SITE 36 (zalafaha) CUT, high. Comma + wa + kana with a NEW delayed subject al-qisas. LAW 1 at full strength. Note also that kana zalafaha is a relative clause trailing kulla sayyiatin, so per LAW 4 the cut goes AFTER the adjunct, not before it, which is exactly where I put it. SITE 40 (al-qisas) CUT, med. Printed wa-kana bada dhalika al-qisasu: al-hasanatu bi-ashri amthaliha. Explicative colon, NOT a quote seam, so my suppression clause does not apply and A4/J1/K3 all say colons cut. Three independent lines converge: the colon, LAW 3 parallelism (al-hasanatu... wa-al-sayyiatu... is a matched pair), and K3's subject-NP-splits-from-predicate-NP caption rule. It also turns one 10-token block into 4 + 6. SITE 46 (dif) CUT, high. Comma + wa + a new topic NP with a nominal predicate. This is LAW 1 and section C4 verbatim, and section L flags wa-plus-appositive-continuation as my single most persistent residual leak. SITE 48 (bi-mithliha) CUT, med. Comma in print before the exceptive illa an yatajawaza Allahu anha. LAW 4 and section B3 both argue for welding a trailing subordinate clause, but both were derived outside hadith, and D2 gives me the direct in-register counter-example: gold cuts fa-in jaa rabbuha fa-adiha ilayhi off as its own segment, a trailing conditional. Hadith matn segments trailing adjuncts. Taking it. SITE 53 (anha) CUT, forced (final token). NEGATIVE CHECKS: no Latin script, no digits, no URLs, no initials, no s.b, so section A2 and checklist item 3 yield nothing here. The salawat formula salla Allah alayhi wa-sallam carries no internal punctuation, so no cut at 19 or 23. No cuts at 39 (al-qisas is the delayed subject of kana), 43, or 45 (bare PPs inside one nominal sentence). RESULT: 10 boundaries over 54 tokens, mean 5.4 tokens per segment, squarely inside the 4-9 band LAW 6 records for this register, and a ~4x increase in cut density over what I would have produced in batch 1.
